chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Why he preferred sitting in to big-band section work
summary: Sitting in gave him freedom to play his own thing, while in big bands the solos were not distributed fairly and the leader or arranger chose who played.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: When you made this sort of switch...you made this switch from big bands to small groups, was that a big change in terms of your own playing? Or was it just because... You said earlier when we were talking the other day that you used to sit in a lot, you used to go take your horn around....
So stretching out a little more might not have been that much of a change. Although....

Well, that's where I'd get my kicks, was sitting in with guys, you know, because you could play your own thing. When you get in those big bands, you're confined to that music. You know? Now and then you get a chance to play, you get a chance to let yourself go. Some bands that I have played in, I guess I wouldn't want to name the names, but they had good soloists there; you know, there was no reason why I should have to take a solo...but they had all the solos. You know what I mean? They wouldn't distribute it around enough, I suppose. So it would be weeks before I would play any kind of solo, because they never would play the piece that my solo was in! You know?
Who decided that? Would it be the leader...?
Oh, I guess it was the leader, I suppose. I don't know. Or the guy that writes the...
The arranger. Because it's up to the leader to give it to you if he wants to.
Would there be a lot of favoritism like that in the bands sometimes?
Well, it seemed that way, you know. But who knows whether the guy is ...(?)... Naturally...
But it might not always be musical considerations, then. It's not who necessarily can play the best.

No. But I mean, you know, that the leader would think a minute. You know, he'd really think, "This guy never gets to play. Let's give him a solo here." You know? Like that, you know? But a lot of times they don't think. You know. The band gets into one trend in its sound, and when that guy leaves, it leaves such a big hole in the band because nobody has had a chance to play none of these things. Then they have to go experimenting again.
